title: Alpha and Omega (Apocalypse 1:8–18)
hook: John on Patmos sees the living one; the letters are cut into the Easter candle

segments.voice: Yesterday, apocalypse: not destruction, but an unveiling. Your line was an unveiling. Today, the vision itself begins.

It's the dark of Holy Saturday night. Outside a church a fire crackles, and a priest holds a tall new candle, the paschal candle, which will stand near the altar through Easter. Following the rite, he may trace a cross into the wax with a stylus: the Greek letter alpha above it, omega below, and the four numbers of the current year, one in each corner. He presses in five grains of incense for the wounds of Christ, and lights it from the fire. Those letters come from the first chapter of the Apocalypse.
screen: `FIRE ON HOLY SATURDAY NIGHT.` → `ALPHA, OMEGA, THIS YEAR.` → `FROM APOCALYPSE ONE.`

segments.voice: Early in the book, God speaks. In the Douay-Rheims: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, saith the Lord God, who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty." Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, omega the last. In English, A to Z. And A to Z means every letter in between too, every word that could ever be spelled. Then John says where he is: on the island of Patmos, for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus. On the Lord's day he hears a voice behind him like a trumpet. He turns and sees seven golden candlesticks, and among them one like the Son of man. White hair like wool. Eyes like a flame. A voice like many waters. A face shining like the sun. John falls at his feet like a dead man. And the figure lays his right hand on him. "Fear not. I am the First and the Last." I was dead, he says, and now I'm alive forever, and I hold the keys of death. Notice the title. In Isaiah, the first and the last is what God calls himself. Here the risen Christ says it. That's why the priest carves those letters into the Easter candle, saying that all time belongs to Christ, and the ages too. This year goes on the same wax. Whatever happens between its first page and its last, it's inside his A to Z.
screen: `A TO Z, AND EVERYTHING BETWEEN.` · `A VOICE BEHIND HIM ON PATMOS.` · `HE FALLS; A HAND LAID ON HIM.` · `THE YEAR CARVED ON THE CANDLE.` · then, large: `I AM ALPHA AND OMEGA.`

segments.voice: With a fingertip, on your palm or a table, slowly trace a capital A as you breathe in, then an omega, a horseshoe shape with little feet, as you breathe out. Then let the space between the two letters hold your day: the beginning, the end, and everything in the middle. If you pray, rest in the line I am the First and the Last; if you don't, just keep tracing and breathing.
Patmos, the island. Where John received the vision of the Apocalypse, including Christ's words: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last. Today's word.
Your line: the first and the last. Alpha above, omega below, and this year in between. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: At the Easter Vigil, the priest marks the new paschal candle with a cross, the letters alpha and omega and the numerals of the year, and may insert five grains of incense; the candle burns at Masses through the Easter season and at baptisms and funerals through the year.

original.note: Greek: the first and last letters of the alphabet (Apocalypse 1:8), carved on the Easter candle.

trapdoor: what you thought: a fancy way to say forever.
what it means: the first and the last letters and everything between: all of time, every day of it, belongs to God.
what a scholar hears: the first and the last is God's title in Isaiah 44:6; the Apocalypse gives it to the risen Christ (1:17).

chat.says: Why are there Greek letters carved on the big Easter candle?
options: Alpha and omega, first and last letters: Christ holds all time, A to Z.
They're the initials of the saint the parish church is named after.
They mark the name of the candle's maker and the city it came from.
chat.meaning: In the Apocalypse, God and then the risen Christ say: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last. All time belongs to Christ.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): the text says the hand was laid 'upon me', not on a shoulder (fixed in teach screen and fork); removed the superlative 'most human moment', 'in many parishes' and the gloss 'a Sunday'; marking the candle now reads as optional ('may').

Easter Vigil: marking the candle with the cross, alpha, omega and the year's numerals, and the five grains of incense, are optional elements in the current Missal. The script describes them as what the priest does; confirm wording (perhaps 'may trace').
The words said while marking the candle are paraphrased ('all time belongs to Christ, and the ages too'); the current English text is not public domain.
Omega described as 'a horseshoe shape with little feet' for the capital Ω. Confirm.
Isaiah 44:6 'the first and the last' as God's title. Confirm.
